title: A Swarm in the Dark
story:
The aurora forecast printout on the corkboard has a circled line in Tomasz's tidy handwriting:

`KP index 8 tonight. Expect every screen on the station, plus the mainland, on the aurora page.`

Beneath it Ingrid has added, in pen: "One container will fall over. Three copies, spread by the engine, one front door for all of them. Use swarm."

Turn this engine into a swarm and publish the `aurora-feed` service on port 8090, with three replicas of `nginx:alpine`.
objectives: Initialise Docker Swarm on this engine
Create the service `aurora-feed` from `nginx:alpine` with `3` replicas
Publish host port `8090` to container port `80` through the service
All three replicas are running and `http://localhost:8090` answers
startingState: A plain engine, not part of any swarm. `nginx:alpine` is already on the machine.
hints: Swarm mode turns one engine into a cluster manager that schedules services rather than single containers. You first switch the mode on, and then describe the service you want kept alive.

`docker swarm init` enables it (add `--advertise-addr 127.0.0.1` if Docker complains about several addresses). Then `docker service create --name NAME --replicas N -p HOST:CONTAINER IMAGE`. `--detach=false` makes the command wait for convergence.

```bash
docker swarm init
docker service create --detach=false \
  --name aurora-feed \
  --replicas 3 \
  -p 8090:80 \
  nginx:alpine
docker service ls
```

validation.description: Swarm mode is active on this engine
Service `aurora-feed` has 3 replicas of `nginx:alpine`, all running

solution: docker swarm init --advertise-addr 127.0.0.1 || docker swarm init
debrief: A service is a desired state, so swarm keeps replacing replicas until reality matches the number you declared. Pro tip: the published port works on every swarm node via the routing mesh, whichever node actually runs a replica.
